statements.text: At least 182 of 300 launches publicly evidence `assumptions-catalogued` (61%, 95% CI 55–66%).
At least 145 of 300 launches publicly evidence `intended-use-defined` (48%, 95% CI 43–54%).
At least 187 of 300 launches publicly evidence `acceptance-criteria-defined` (62%, 95% CI 57–68%).
At least 129 of 300 launches publicly evidence `failure-modes-tested` (43%, 95% CI 38–49%).
At least 102 of 300 launches publicly evidence `limitations-stated` (34%, 95% CI 29–40%).
At least 53 of 300 launches publicly evidence `operational-owner-assigned` (18%, 95% CI 14–22%).
At least 105 of 300 launches publicly evidence `assurance-defined` (35%, 95% CI 30–41%).
At least 197 of 300 launches publicly evidence `fallback-defined` (66%, 95% CI 60–71%).
At least 152 of 300 launches publicly evidence `recovery-tested` (51%, 95% CI 45–56%).
At least 31 of 300 launches publicly evidence `support-maintenance-defined` (10%, 95% CI 7–14%).
At least 200 of 300 launches publicly evidence `outcome-measure-defined` (67%, 95% CI 61–72%).
At least 187 of 300 launches publicly evidence `baseline-defined` (62%, 95% CI 57–68%).
At least 166 of 300 launches publicly evidence `outcome-measured` (55%, 95% CI 50–61%).
At least 36 of 300 launches publicly evidence `measurement-definition-consistent` (12%, 95% CI 9–16%).
At least 128 of 300 launches publicly evidence `important-confounds-named` (43%, 95% CI 37–48%).
At least 139 of 300 launches publicly evidence `outcome-evidence-available` (46%, 95% CI 41–52%).
At least 51 of 300 launches publicly evidence `full-cost-accounted` (17%, 95% CI 13–22%).
At least 98 of 300 launches publicly evidence `risk-tradeoffs-assessed` (33%, 95% CI 28–38%).
At least 119 of 300 launches publicly evidence `alternatives-compared` (40%, 95% CI 34–45%).
At least 160 of 300 launches publicly evidence `value-rule-explicit` (53%, 95% CI 48–59%).
At least 179 of 300 launches publicly evidence enough checks for the deterministic gate to support the `explore` decision on public evidence (60%, 95% CI 54–65%).
Reported descriptively: at least one source has fewer than 30 included launches, so the pre-registered test was not run. The Holm correction covers the remaining hypotheses.

H1 (a majority of launches claim at least one check without linking an artefact, so they do not publicly evidence it) is supported: 287 of 300 launches (96%), one-sided exact binomial, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001; with the recall bound, 256 of 300, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001.

H3 (fewer than half of launches publicly evidence at least one `rely`-decision check) is not supported: at least 275 of 300 launches (92%) publicly evidence one, one-sided exact binomial, Holm-adjusted p = 1.000; with the recall bound, 300 of 300, Holm-adjusted p = 1.000.
Each headline figure is repeated excluding the 4 launches whose site could not be read (protocol section 3).

Each cohort is the launches of one quarter, described by what they publicly evidence today. Older launches have had longer to publish, and launches that disappeared are not in the sample, so these figures are not a trend and are not compared as one.

Agent roles, no human edits.
A launch is included when it is an AI product with its own site, screened in two stages: first its title and URL, then the text of its own page.
The sampling frame is Show HN posts in the sampling window, 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, drawn in a seeded order.
Evidence is collected from each launch's own site and own repository only.
A check counts as publicly evidenced only when the launch's own page quotes it and links an artefact; a quote with no linked artefact is coded as claimed.

Every positive is confirmed by a confirmer that did not code it before it enters any figure. A rejected positive counts as not evidenced and stays in the denominator; a downgraded pass counts as claimed.
The deterministic gate, not a model, decides each decision from the confirmed check states.

Every figure is a count of launches under disclosure control: a count, its complement or its group size under 10 is suppressed, and an exact audit requires at least 5 possible values for every suppressed count.

H1 and H3 use one-sided exact binomial tests and H2 a permutation test with Cramér's V. Holm's correction holds the family-wise level at 0.05, and a hypothesis is supported only when it also holds with the measured collection recall as a bound.
Screening missed its pre-registered target: 12.2% of audited exclusions were in error (5 of 41, 95% CI 5.3–25.5%) against a 10% bar. This is a selection limitation.
A re-measure at 2.4% is exploratory: the rule was tightened on the same 41 cases and was not re-applied to the 300.
Supported recall 0.894 (59 of 66; 8 of 10 projects contributed); raw recall 0.887 (141 of 159).
Of 159 gathered items, 66 (42%) were supported and 93 (58%) unsupported, 27 (17%) of them boilerplate such as calls to action.
The paid search collector was replaced by a free own-site collector for all bulk coding (addendum A8), so every launch was collected the same way.

Exploratory: on 142 projects the free and the paid collectors agree at a positive-level agreement of about 0.78. The all-states agreement of 0.915 is raised by states both found nothing for and is not the headline.

A collector defect produced whole-page evidence spans. Every project was re-segmented into spans of at most 1,500 characters, and the decisions made on the defective spans are archived as exploratory and feed no published figure (addendum A9).

Every role is an agent: screener (synthetic-model-a on synthetic-host-1); coder (synthetic-model-b on synthetic-host-2); second coder (synthetic-model-c on synthetic-host-1); independent labeller (synthetic-model-d on synthetic-host-1); confirmer (synthetic-model-e on synthetic-host-1); screening auditor (synthetic-model-d on synthetic-host-1); recall gatherer (synthetic-model-f on synthetic-host-3); sign-off reviewer (synthetic-model-g on synthetic-host-3).
